original.guitar: Patrick Bourgeois or Alain Lapointe (the credits for this track were not found)
original.amp: Unknown. Typical late-80s pop-rock studio clean: bright, chorused, stereo delay
original.effects: Chorus, stereo delay, hall reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: From the debut album Les BB (1989). No source documents the gear on this song, so this tone follows the style of the record.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the clean, chorused parts and arpeggios. Switch to channel B for a light AC30 crunch where the song needs more push. COMP is off. Turn it on, low, if arpeggios need more sustain. The chorus and delay are stereo: pan the Tonelab's L and R apart on the mixer.
recipes.why: Late-80s pop-rock guitar sits behind the synths as a bright clean sound with deep chorus, a stereo delay and a big hall reverb. Both pickups, split, give a glassy, Strat-like middle-position sound.

original.amp: Unknown. Typical late-80s polished rock lead: Marshall-style amp
original.effects: Light chorus, long stereo delay, hall reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: From the debut album Les BB (1989). No source documents the gear on this song, so this tone follows the style of the record.

recipes.tips: Channel A for melodic lead lines, channel B for the solo. The neck humbucker keeps it round and singing. Switch to the bridge if it gets lost under the keyboards. Stomp the Tube OD for more sustain.
recipes.why: The polished late-80s lead sound: a JCM800-style crunch, a touch of chorus, a long stereo delay that ducks under the playing, and a hall reverb.
